## Findings
- claim-1: For \(q=n-r\), \(J_v\subset\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) satisfy \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Put \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(q=n-r\), and \[ v^\vee=v_{q,n-s,q-s+t,n}=v_{q,\ q-i+j,\ q-i+1,\ n}. \] Then \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian: \(q-i\ge0\) follows from \(t>r+s-n\); hence \(1\le q-i+1\le q\), \(q-i+1\le q-i+j=n-s\), and \[ (q-i+1)-\bigl(q+(n-s)-n\bigr)=t>0. \] Its parameters are \(i^\vee=j,\ j^\vee=i,\ a^\vee=a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), and \(b^\vee=b=\min(i,j)\).
- claim-3: Writing \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), the integral Schur involution induces \[ \bar\omega:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}, \qquad\bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}, \] because \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\). Basiswise, \[ \bar\omega(J_v) =\bigoplus_{j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu =J_{v^\vee}. \]
- claim-4: The 2024 theorem assumes precisely a bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), defines \(i,j,a,b\), works in the integral quotient \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and proves minimality of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110]
- claim-5: Applying Theorem 1.2 to \(v^\vee\) gives minimality of \[ \{\bar s_\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}\subset J_{v^\vee}. \] Pullback under \(\bar\omega^{-1}\) is the minimally generating family \[ \boxed{\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}} \subset J_v, \] since \((j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\). Thus the transposed family is minimal, including degenerate \(a=0\) cases (with zero-length blocks omitted).
- claim-6: No independent critic or skeptic review record was supplied; therefore no post-review horizontal continuation can be certified.
## Strategy
1. Let \(q=n-r\), with \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Set
   \[
   i=s-t+1,\qquad j=r-t+1.
   \]
   Then \(i,j\ge1\), \(q-i=n-r-s+t-1\ge0\), and \(r-j=t-1\ge0\). Also \(r<n\) and \(s<n\), since \(r=n\) or \(s=n\) contradicts \(t\le s,r\) and \(t>r+s-n\).

2. Define
   \[
   v^\vee=v_{q,n-s,q-s+t,n}
   =v_{q,\ q-i+j,\ q-i+1,\ n}.
   \]
   Its parameters satisfy
   \[
   r^\vee=q,\quad s^\vee=n-s=q-i+j,\quad t^\vee=q-i+1.
   \]
   Explicitly,
   \[
   1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,\qquad
   1\le t^\vee\le s^\vee,\qquad
   1\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n,
   \]
   using \(q-i\ge0\), \(i,j\ge1\), \(q,n-s\ge1\). Moreover
   \[
   t^\vee-\bigl(r^\vee+s^\vee-n\bigr)
   =(q-s+t)-(q-s)=t>0.
   \]
   Hence \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian.

3. The transformed parameters are
   \[
   i^\vee=j,\qquad j^\vee=i,\qquad
   a^\vee=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b^\vee=\min(j,i)=b.
   \]

4. Since Schur functions are an integral basis and
   \(I_{r,q}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of the Schur functions outside
   \(q^r\), \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\) is a
   \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\)
   [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 89-94].  The cited generator formula is
   \[
   \{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\}
   \]
   [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document].
   Its span is an ideal: LR terms in
   \(\bar s_\theta\bar s_\mu\) have \(\mu\subseteq\nu\), and only
   \(\nu\subseteq q^r\) survive [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 136-142].
   Therefore
   \[
   J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda.
   \]
   Applying the same argument to \(v^\vee\) gives
   \[
   J_{v^\vee}=
   \bigoplus_{j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu.
   \]

5. Define the integral Schur involution by
   \(\omega(e_k)=h_k\); it is a \(\mathbb Z\)-algebra involution and
   \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\).  Since
   \[
   \lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q,
   \]
   it maps \(I_{r,q}\) exactly onto \(I_{q,r}\), inducing
   \[
   \bar\omega:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}.
   \]
   On the displayed bases,
   \[
   \bar\omega(J_v)
   =\bigoplus_{j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu
   =J_{v^\vee}.
   \]

6. Theorem 1.2 applies to \(v^\vee\): it is bigrassmannian, works over
   the integral quotient, and gives minimality of
   \[
   \{\bar s_\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}
   \subset J_{v^\vee}
   \]
   [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110].

7. Conjugating the upper partition gives
   \[
   (j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{\,j-b});
   \]
   this follows by counting columns: the first \(b\) have height \(i+a\),
   and the remaining \(j-b\) have height \(i\). Pullback through
   \(\bar\omega^{-1}\), which preserves proper containment of generated
   ideals, proves minimality of
   \[
   \{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
   \subset J_v.
   \]
   If \(a=0\), this is \(i^j\); zero-length blocks are omitted.

8. No new literature or provider search is used.
